degraded.detail: external_review.py --mode code: the openai leg returned a full 9-finding review; the gemini leg returned status=success with feedback=null, so only one of two external code reviewers actually reported. Recorded rather than counted as two.
degraded.impact: single-reviewer external code coverage; compensated by the internal code-reviewer and doubt-reviewer passes, both of which found defects the external leg did not

degraded.detail: The first --mode code attempt against the full 1691-line diff returned 29 chars (openai) and 504 chars (gemini) — truncated, not a review. Re-run against a 773-line production-code-only diff. Consequence disclosed: the narrowed slice excluded the wiring and test files, which produced two false 'high' findings (tool wired to nothing / no tests exist).

surface_verification.justification: No startable app surface: the change alters two build-time artifact producers inside the framework's own Python tooling — no server, no end-user CLI entry point, no UI. Verified instead by the full F0 suite plus three empirical probes that ran the REAL producers end to end (update_compliance.py regenerating all five evidence documents; stamp_test_results.py against the repo's own tracked record; Group E staleness against the stamped documents).

behaviors.behavior: the markdown banner round-trips to its abbreviated form
all three dirty states survive the banner, so a clean tree and an unanswerable one do not render alike
the JSON block round-trips exactly, keeping the full 40-hex commit
unresolved fields serialise as null rather than being omitted
arbitrary garbage read back yields an empty state, never a half-trusted one
a run id cannot forge a second banner line
a whitespace-bearing run id cannot inject a forged status token
Unicode control, format and line-separator characters are refused
an unsubstituted {run_id} template placeholder is refused rather than stamped
a run id containing the word clean or cleanup does not forge a dirty verdict
the commit is validated on both sides, and a run id is never read back as a commit
the strip regex is anchored: document body prose, layout blank lines and CRLF all survive
git resolution distinguishes clean, tracked-modified, untracked-only, and the excluded stamped artifact
git absent, timing out, non-repo or an empty repo all degrade to null instead of raising
git is never invoked through a shell and always with a bounded timeout
the stamp writes code-resolved run id, commit and dirty into the test-results record
every other top-level key keeps its value and its position
the record is serialised in the repo canonical byte form, with no CRLF
stamping twice equals stamping once; a prior block is replaced, never nested
a corrupt, array-shaped or missing record is refused and never overwritten
a rejected run id stamps null instead of falling back to a plausible wrong one
all five compliance evidence documents carry exactly one Source-State line, directly under Generated
the run id and the timestamp are read off one work event, so the two header lines cannot disagree
Group E staleness cannot newly report a document stale because of the banner, and still detects real body drift
behaviors.evidence: test_source_state_stamp.py::TestGroupEStalenessUnaffected (5 cases) PASSED; plus an empirical Group E run proving the banner is absent from normalize() output for all five documents

behaviors.behavior: an ADR reference recorded in adr_id is never labelled as a run
audit_staleness stays importable when loaded by file path from a foreign scripts namespace
behaviors.evidence: test_source_state_stamp.py::TestAuditStalenessStaysFilePathLoadable::test_no_module_level_cross_package_import PASSED; plus the real file-path loaders in shipwright-security (6) and shared (5) sessions PASSED

behaviors.behavior: a repeat render of the same data is byte-identical, so tracked documents do not go permanently dirty
git C-quotes a non-ASCII porcelain path, which can defeat the dirty exclusion
behaviors.reason: The failure direction is fail-safe — it over-reports modification and can never under-report — and it is unreachable for the ASCII repo-root path both producers use. Raised by the doubt reviewer, accepted and disclosed in the spec's resolution contract rather than silently relied on; the exclusion mechanism itself is pinned by TestGitResolution.
